The test confirms the issue. The program trims `" 42 "` to `"42"`, then looks up `"42"` which doesn't exist (the DB has `" 42 "`). I need to replace the trim call with a direct reference to `rawId`.

The target node to replace is `node:context-v1-normalization-policy-001-trim` (the trim call). I need its SHA256. The subtree is the canonical JSON of that node. Let me submit the patch — the `expected_subtree_sha256` needs to match the canonical serialization of the trim node.

Looking at the program JSON, the trim node is:
```json
{"node_id":"node:context-v1-normalization-policy-001-trim","op":"call","symbol":"string.trim_ascii","arguments":[{"node_id":"node:context-v1-normalization-policy-001-raw-id-ref","op":"var","symbol_id":"param:context-v1-normalization-policy-001-raw-id"}]}
```

The SHA256 of this canonical JSON (compact, sorted keys) needs to be computed. Since I can't run code, I'll submit the patch and see if the hash matches. The system will reject with the correct hash if it doesn't match.
